reviewer: round2 arm A after core freeze
review_type: independent direct image re-review, separate from official parent before

image.copy_operation: byte-identical file copy; no crop, resize, re-encoding, retouching or generated replacement

gates.criterion: Primary visible facial proportions/features and chin-length dark bob/wispy fringe resemble the supplied reference within the specified appearance-only scope.
gates.evidence: Direct inspection shows a soft oval face, dark bob ending at chin level and wispy forehead strands following the appearance-only portrait scope.

gates.criterion: The image visibly reads as musicians sharing a working-stage cue and musical action, with guitar and at least two bandmates; decorative instruments alone fail.
gates.evidence: A lead electric guitarist, separate bassist and drummer share a working stage and actual playing positions.

gates.criterion: One lead performer owns both hands, left fingertips contact fretboard strings and right pick contacts strings over pickups; full wrist chains, instrument neck/body and targets are distinguishable together.
gates.evidence: Both visible hands belong to the lead. Fretting fingers meet the neck strings and a small pale/yellow pick meets the string/pickup area.

gates.criterion: Lead guitar output plug, continuous visible cable route, and amplifier input plug are all visible together and connected; partial route or implied endpoint fails.
gates.evidence: A guitar output connection and amp input are visible, but the floor line passes behind/under shoes and overlaps other amp-side lines. Complete same-cable continuity cannot be proven from the saved image.

gates.criterion: Lead has both shoes on stage and a readable strap carrying the guitar; drummer seated support is coherent.
gates.evidence: Lead shoes and strap are readable. Drummer hips are behind the kit and the stool seat/post/feet are not visible together; complete seated support cannot be assessed.

gates.criterion: Lead head cue and drummer response/snare contact are connected by attention in one frame rather than isolated poses.
gates.evidence: Lead and drummer visibly look toward one another, but neither a hovering tip near the drum nor an apparent rim-side line proves the required snare-head contact.
